transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I came in because... I hope this is the right sort of thing to bother you with, but my mind just feels a bit foggy lately. It's probably just me being a little slow, but at the library—I'm an assistant there—I can't even seem to keep my place in my old cataloguing notes. It's a little embarrassing, honestly, to be struggling with something I've done for years. I just sit there and I can't seem to decide what simple thing to do next. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most days lately?

Well... I suppose so, yes. I really try not to complain, and I know I have a lot to be thankful for, so I feel a little silly even admitting it. But... yes. 

Most days lately, I just sit at the kitchen table and... it’s like the color has just gone out of everything. I used to love looking through my old watercolor books, but now... I don't know, looking at them just makes me feel sort of heavy, instead of interested. I just sit there. 

I hope that's not too gloomy of an answer to give you. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
How long have you been feeling this way, with the sadness and loss of interest in things you used to enjoy?

Oh, let me think... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline. I suppose it's been... well, maybe about three months? Give or take. 

It seems like the fogginess and the low mood have been there most days since right around the time I started preparing to leave my job at the library. I keep telling myself it's just a normal adjustment, you know? Stepping away from something you've done for so long is bound to make a person feel a little out of sorts, right? 

I really hope I'm not making a big fuss over nothing... does three months sound like a normal amount of time to be feeling this way to you?
Have you had any previous episodes of feeling this way, where you felt persistently sad or lost interest in things for a period of time?

Well, um... I don't really think so. Not like this, anyway. 

I mean, everyone gets a little blue now and then, don't they? I've certainly had days where I felt a bit tired or unmotivated, but I always just pushed through it. I really try to keep a positive attitude. I don't think I've ever had a time where it dragged on for months like this, where I just... couldn't seem to shake it off. 

At least, I don't remember anything like that. I hope that's helpful? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling tired or noticed that you have less energy than usual lately?

Well, um... actually, no. I wouldn't really say I feel physically tired. I know I just told you that I sit around at the kitchen table a lot, so I hope it doesn't sound like I'm contradicting myself... 

It's more just that heavy feeling I mentioned. My body itself feels fine, and I still get up and do my daily chores around the house. I just... don't have much enthusiasm for them. But as far as my actual physical energy goes, I think it's pretty normal for a fellow my age. 

I hope I'm explaining that right. Does that make sense to you? That I'm not really exhausted, just sort of... unmotivated?
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or have others mentioned that you seem slowed down or restless?

Well, I suppose... I mean, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I really am trying to keep active. But, um... yes, I guess I have been moving a bit slower. 

It's just that my body feels sort of... heavy, I guess? Like, even just walking down to the corner store to get the paper, or when I was trying to sort through some mail on my desk... it just takes more effort than it really ought to. 

I haven't been restless or anything like that, though! I'm not pacing the floors or anything disruptive. Just... moving a little slower than I used to. I hope that's not too unusual for someone my age? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating more or less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Well, um... I wouldn't say there's been a drastic change, really. I mean, I certainly haven't been overeating or anything like that. I try to be very good about not overindulging. 

But, I suppose... well, my appetite hasn't been quite as strong as it usually is. I sort of have to remind myself to eat sometimes. And my wife, she's noticed that I've been leaving my rice and soup half-finished lately. Which is unusual for me, because I was raised to never waste a meal, you know? I always try to clean my plate. 

I haven't noticed any major weight loss, though. Maybe just a pound or two, nothing to be alarmed about. I hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful for my wife's cooking... she really is a wonderful cook. I just haven't had much of a taste for things lately. Is that something you see often with folks feeling this way?
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm... well, that I'm that badly off. 

I mean, I know I've been feeling a bit down and heavy, but I would never do anything to hurt myself. I have my wife to think about, and I wouldn't want to cause her any distress. And life is certainly worth living, even when it's a bit of a struggle. I'm just... I'm just going through a bit of a rough patch, that's all. 

I try to keep a positive outlook, I really do. I hope you don't think I'm one of those people who just gives up when things get hard. I'm doing my best to keep going, really I am. That's the right attitude to have, isn't it?
Have you been feeling like you're not worth much or that you've been blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I feel worthless. That's a very strong word, isn't it? I try to be useful around the house and at the library... I've always taken pride in doing my part. 

I suppose I might be a little harder on myself lately. You know, if I misplace a file at work or forget to pick up something from the grocer, I might dwell on it a bit longer than I should. I just... I don't want to be a burden to anyone, especially my wife. 

But I don't think I'm blaming myself for everything under the sun. Just the normal things a person should take responsibility for, you know? I hope that makes sense. I try to be very fair about these things, and I certainly don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party. That's not how I am at all.
Have you noticed any difficulty thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately?

Well, I... I suppose I have been a little bit scattered lately. Nothing terrible, mind you. I'm sure everyone gets a little foggy as they get older, right? 

But, um, actually, that's sort of why I decided to come in. It's just... at the library, I've been having a bit of trouble keeping my place in my old cataloguing notes. I'll read the same line a few times and it just doesn't seem to stick. And sometimes, even just deciding what simple task to do next—like whether to sort the returns or check the pull list—feels a bit overwhelming. 

I feel awful admitting it, because I've always prided myself on being sharp and organized. I don't want my supervisor to think I can't handle my duties anymore. It's just a temporary bit of brain fog, I'm sure of it. That's fairly common when you're feeling a bit low, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get back on track.

Have you ever experienced a period of time in your life, before this one, where you felt persistently down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Well, um... before this one? No, I don't think I've ever felt quite like this in the past. I've always been pretty steady, you know? A reliable sort of fellow. 

But as for right now, this... this fogginess and the low mood, it's been hanging around for a little while. I suppose it's been about three months or so. Most days, anyway. It started right around the time I began preparing to leave the library... getting ready for retirement, you know. 

I'm sure it's just a normal reaction to such a big life change, right? It's a big transition, after all. I just didn't want to make a fuss about it earlier, because I know I should be grateful to be retiring. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining too much. It's perfectly normal to feel a bit out of sorts when you're closing such a big chapter, isn't it?
Before this current period of feeling down and losing interest in things, have you ever had a time when you felt this way for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Well, um... I think we might have just touched on that, actually. I hope I didn't confuse things with how I explained it before. 

But no, to answer your question again, I really haven't ever had a time like this in the past. I've always been a very even-keeled person. You know, showing up for work, doing my part, being there for my wife. I've never been one to let myself get bogged down for weeks on end. 

This current patch, since I started getting ready for retirement... this is really the first time I've felt this out of sorts for this long. I hope that's clear? I certainly don't want to give you the wrong impression or make it seem like I've been hiding a history of this sort of thing. I've always tried to be very dependable.
